Apple Card celebrates its seventh anniversary this month, with features that have continued to improve over the years. These include new functionalities, new offers, and new rewards. In addition, a major change is on the horizon.

Here's a roundup of all the latest developments with Apple Card.

iOS 27: Recurring Transactions

As my colleague Ryan mentioned last month, iOS 27 adds a very useful new "Recurring" feature to Apple Card in the Wallet app. You can find the "Recurring" section by tapping the three-dot menu in the top right corner.

Within this menu, you'll see a list of recurring transactions that will soon be charged to your Apple Card, including the estimated transaction date and amount. In addition to the list view, you can also browse month by month in the calendar view mode.

For Apple Card users on iOS 27, this is a pretty handy new feature. It's already available in the public beta and developer versions, and is expected to officially launch for all users next month.

New Membership Benefit

Earlier this month, Apple added a new offer for Apple Card users who travel frequently.

Apple has partnered with Booking.com: all Apple Card users who complete a stay or car rental can earn "Genius Level 2" membership status. Users will also earn 3% Daily Cash on all Booking.com purchases.

So what are the perks of "Genius Level 2" membership? Apple says your status can "unlock a range of benefits at participating stays and car rentals, such as 10–15% discounts, free breakfast, and room upgrades."

Hertz Partnership

Last year, Apple announced a partnership with Hertz, offering exclusive perks for users who book car rentals with Apple Card:

  • Free emergency roadside assistance
  • Option to add damage waiver coverage at a discounted rate of $16.95 per day (before tax).
  • Free additional driver added at the time of pickup.
  • A minimum 5% discount on Pay Later base rental rates.

In addition, car rentals booked through Hertz and paid with Apple Card earn 3% Daily Cash.

Apple Card Savings Account Feature Expansion

One criticism of Apple Card has long been that many important account management features require an iPhone to use. Since Apple Card launched, Apple has been working to improve this.

Recently, Apple added web-based login for the Apple Card savings account. This means you can now view and manage your Apple Card savings account directly through a web browser.

Major Change on the Horizon

However, the biggest change for Apple Card right now is the upcoming transition from Goldman Sachs to Chase. Apple announced this deal back in January, saying at the time that the transition period would be "approximately 24 months."

There are still many unknowns about Apple Card's future under Chase. Apple has promised that several important elements of Apple Card will remain unchanged after Chase takes over. Over the next 18 months, Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Apple will continue to work out the details, and we should see more concrete information emerge.

Wrap-Up

Are you an Apple Card holder? What do you think of the card? Personally, I think it's a great option for users in the Apple ecosystem, although you can usually find more generous rewards in other ecosystems. For my own part, I use Apple Card to pay for my Apple subscription services to earn 3% Daily Cash. The option to buy Apple hardware at 0% interest installments is also very appealing.

Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
